intro: Paste the model with every input and its source, your data interrogation, your weakest assumption and its sensitivity, then the 250–350 word write-up including your position on this module's claim. Resubmission is free and unlimited: the score is a mirror, not a gate.
activityContext: You are grading a learner submission for AI 301 · The Specialist, HRBP track. Module 5 applied activity, 'One case, stress-tested': a real unresolved argument built into one of three models (regretted attrition, cost of an extra layer, time-to-fill against plan), with every input's source and provenance shown, an explicit statement of where AI was and wasn't used, an interrogation of how each HR-system field is actually populated versus what its name implies, at least one named input they don't fully trust with what they did about it, and their weakest assumption named FIRST with a plausible range and the conclusion tested at the unfavourable end. CRITICAL: a case that fails its own sensitivity test and is reported honestly scores HIGHER than one that passes because it was never tested. Also watch for the module's central failure, small populations carrying percentage claims; if the learner's denominator is small, they must state the n and volunteer the coincidence test. False precision should be marked down; a rough figure with stated assumptions is the target. Grade the delta, never prediction accuracy.

opening.label: Predicted — cost of one regretted departure, mid-level role
opening.hint: Whole currency units. Gut estimate, before any arithmetic.

calibration.label: Built — what your model actually says
calibration.hint: Including the productivity ramp, which most estimates omit.

dimensions.name: The model has a visible skeleton
dimensions.criteria: Every input shown with its source, arithmetic followable, and AI's contribution stated honestly (structure and sensitivity yes; supplied numbers no). Rough figures with stated assumptions are the target; false precision to the pound reads as naivety or concealment and should be marked down.

dimensions.name: The data was interrogated
dimensions.criteria: For each HR-system input, how the field is actually populated versus what its name implies, with at least one input named as not fully trusted and a stated response. A learner who writes 'I don't know how regretted is set, and that's my first question for analytics' scores well; one who uses the field uncritically does not.

dimensions.name: Small numbers handled honestly
dimensions.criteria: Where the population is small, the n appears in the sentence with the finding, percentages are not used to imply a larger denominator, and a coincidence test is volunteered. Where the population genuinely cannot support a quantified claim, saying so and making the qualitative case explicitly is the top-scoring response.

dimensions.name: It argues against itself first
dimensions.criteria: The weakest assumption named before any strengths, with a plausible range and the conclusion tested at the unfavourable end. A case that does not survive its own test, reported plainly, scores at the top of this dimension. Also grades the position on the module's claim, including its counter-argument that influence runs through relationships and trust rather than analysis.
